brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.evidence: 7 full bases at level 0: centre piece:0,0,0;full plus its 6 neighbours (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0); check_build shows all 7 in one group.

requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes
requirements.evidence: 3 stud-variant spikes placed via stud spike sockets: spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0, spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1, spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0, spread across the cluster as feet.
Each spike was applied from a stud socket with facing:"down" and accepted with no refusal.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb: one centre full base ringed by six full bases at level 0, standing on three downward-facing stud spikes spread across the cluster (west, north-east and south-east junctions). House rules applied — open faces capped with 18 solid caps and 12 joint bolts locked the joints. check_build passes with no issues and meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Seven-cell honeycomb on stud feet — checking the current build and spike options.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: Seven cells are in place. Now finding downward stud spike sites for the feet.
Three downward stud feet are on. Now applying the house rules — capping open faces and locking joints.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.

events.text: From above all seven cells read as one honeycomb and the check is clear. Let me also confirm the feet from a low angle.
